Yeah I got a few seeds in all of them actually and probably a few more in the actual God X widow. I think it was mostly the stress from losing my pH probe during Week 6, and maybe also bending them down in week 3.

But the system also has problems and I've already trashed it. I'm in the midst of swapping over to a shallow water wave culture setup that's improved in a number of ways for a much happier root zone.

I consider the previous setup a wrong fork, as well as half assed. Even had a mold donut around one of the stalks and that's the second such incident after I made a number of improvements and ran it reasonably well. I'm transplanting some clones back into the tent now and had a look at the roots of the new setup last night. Looks very promising. Plucking leaves from them leaves the fingers all sticky and there's a shitload more leaves to pluck with overall faster and denser growth. They smell much better. So I'm looking forward to seeing how they yield given the same genetics and a very similar environment.

I predict that given a cooler root zone with far greater exposure to available oxygen, the buds will form up better rather than slowly fox tail the whole way and hopefully produce more yield faster with some real stinkers. Even though the bud that I got cured up great..excellent quality and the highs are all excellent, the plants weren't exactly tear jerkers. They will be now.

I used a combination of Maxi Bloom with Pure Blend Pro Bloom Soil. Additives: Liquid Karma, Protekt for silicates, Cal-Mag product up to ~200ppm, and I think about a mL of Floralicious Plus for ~50 gallons. Along with some tea here and there which was always a mistake, Hydroguard, and Myko Grow.

Since that system used the netpots as bio filters, along with the roots populating them, they get caked up and I believe choked the plants off. I believe full submersion in unchilled water did the same. In some cases, and apparently not uncommon, the roots never really escaped the netpots at all. That's unacceptable. This system was designed to push the water flow up through the rootball, and so you'd think intuitively it should have great flow through it with no stagnant zones but the opposite is true. The steady upwards flow keeps the roots inside the pot. If they escape at all it's usually just around the edge by the water line. While the media and roots in them become suffocated in otherwise beneficial slime. Buckets with the highest flow end up having the worst root production. They generally all stay small and hair like with no larger, bulkier, rope like 'water roots'. Meanwhile the densest zone of the rootball right at the base where it originally branched out like crazy from the air pruning was the most suffocated from the most stagnant flow, completely lost in slop.

One solution to that is to adopt the rule of 'no teas, no organics, hydro pure'. That's true to some extent but plants do love the extras and it results in superior flavors and aromas as well as yield so I think that's a wrong course of action. A chiller would be an additional huge expense that wouldn't resolve the flow issues stagnating root development.

So after run #2 with a series of whatever improvements I could do that were feasible, like upgrading the pump's volute plate for improved flow/pressure to boost the Venturi air intake and the 'ram air' scoops to vent the rez which at least allowed it all to run at ambient, and overall ran it smoother throughout, I got me knife cut the fucking hoses off and tossed em in the trash.

From what I've seen the ultimate stability achievable of such a system is a myth. While the lack of ultimate stability in more dynamic systems like with DWC/Bubble Buckets, doesn't seem to impede their performance. Even with greatly extended maintenance requirements resulting in drastically shorter light hours. Mind you, this has been my best yield to date. Yielding isn't usually my main priority either so it doesn't mean that much but as you saw with the bud structure/development and I think also yield.. it's too pathetic. The terpene production should be utterly offensive and it wasn't. So it's too pathetic overall when 'ultimate stability' never delivers and I'm moving on. I'm in the midst of restocking the tent with the new setup now and looking forward to superior results with it.

It's also a much simpler, quieter, cost effective system with greater modularity, that will facilitate experimentation/troubleshooting and so on. In a perpetual grow style that is also more tolerant of higher temps. Perhaps the greatest benefit of the new setup is that it's no longer modeled after someone called 'HurtBack'.. and I won't have to swap 50 gallons out each week.

I'll probably post a few more pictures of the last harvest and the new setup later.

Cheers
